witness.note: 009000 dates the main surviving Sumerian copies to the early second millennium BCE, leaving the earlier story’s origin unknown. Numeric bounds retain whole-millennium precision.
witness.label: Early 2nd millennium BCE · surviving Sumerian copies

description: Follows Inanna through the seven gates of the underworld, her death, Ninshubur’s persistent appeals, Enki’s rescue and Dumuzi’s substitution and the sharing of time below with Geshtinanna. Compares the Sumerian and Akkadian descents and examines sovereignty, ritual thresholds, loyalty, compassionate negotiation and the poem’s use of repetition without assuming a single seasonal or astronomical allegory.
